question: Can a dependency-valid post-vision IR make adapter-version recompilation materially cheaper than rebuilding a multimodal index from images without changing the resulting index?

methods.raw_full: Decode/process the source image, execute vision, then execute the complete language suffix and projection.
methods.ir_full: Load a materialized post-vision input-embedding IR, then execute the complete language suffix and projection.
methods.raw_l12: Decode/process the source image, execute vision, then compile visual states at language layer 12 before the remaining suffix.
methods.ir_l12: Load a materialized post-vision input-embedding IR, then compile visual states at language layer 12 before the remaining suffix.

measurement.raw_source: In-memory compressed image bytes from the already-open Parquet corpus; image decode and processor execution are timed.
measurement.ir_source: One torch-serialized shard per minibatch; file load and host-to-device transfer are timed.
measurement.interpretation: IR measurements are warm-storage recompilation measurements because the operating-system page cache is not flushed. No cold-NVMe claim is permitted.

dependency_contract.adapter_update: The reusable IR is valid, but cached terminal document embeddings are invalid.
dependency_contract.policy_only_update: Cached terminal document embeddings are valid and are the stronger baseline; ReprForge must not claim an advantage from replaying the suffix.
dependency_contract.vision_or_processor_update: The reusable IR is invalid and compilation falls back to the raw source.

gates.semantic_equivalence: raw and IR paths must be tensor-identical for the same Full or L12 method, or have max absolute error <= 1e-6
gates.storage_diagnostic: Report compressed source-image, reusable-IR, Full-index, and L12-index bytes per page; do not hide IR amplification.

claim_boundary: This experiment isolates adapter/projection-version recompilation on one model and one page shape. It can validate a mechanism and payoff, but cannot establish cross-model, cross-benchmark, cold-storage, or end-to-end version-control generality.
